question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>}</mo></math> and let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo></math>denote the power set of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>. If the number of functions <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>)</mo></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>A</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>m</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>N</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is least, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></math> is equal to ______.

solution.text:
Given,

A={1,2,3,….7}

And f:A→P(A) and a∈A

Also a∈f(a), that means ‘a’ will be the element of subset as f:A→P(A),

Now, total options for 1 will be 26. (Because 26 subsets contains elements1)

Similarly, for every other element we get, total  26×26×26×26×26×26×26=242 subsets.

Now, comparing with mn we get, m=2 & n=42

Hence,  m+n=2+42=44
